_doc: The numbers the lab DERIVES by measurement on its rigs, stated as data rather than as literals in code. Filed 2026-09-12 to close the gap the per-rig-numbers task named: several rig- or engine-specific measured values were hard-coded in `src/`, so the number lived where the measurement's provenance could not, and nothing would notice it drifting from the rig it described. This file is the lab's record of each value and why it is that value. `mcgyvr.derived` reads no file under `tools/`: it answers from a user's own `numbers.yaml` first and from the product's shipped estimates (`data/numbers.json`) second, and a number neither states is a named refusal, never a silent inline default. The lab's tests write this record into that user's file in each test's HOME (`tests/lab_numbers.py`), so a lab test judges with these values: a value the product ships may change without failing one, while a class the product adds fails the lab's check until this file records it. `tools/runs/hosts.json` is the sibling declaration of what each rig IS (read live by gate 2); this file states what was MEASURED for it. It is JSON and content-addressable so a reader can digest it the way it digests `hosts.json`.
_numbers_doc: Per-host `numbers` blocks: a value recorded for that rig, measured on it or declared from another rig's measurement where its `why` says so. This is the lab's record; `mcgyvr.derived` does not read it. It answers from a user's own `numbers.yaml` first and from the product's shipped estimates in `data/numbers.json` second, keyed by tolerance class or engine and never by a rig's name.

runtime_resident_gb.why: Host RAM beyond the spilled experts themselves (context, compute buffers, copy paths). Swept across six --n-cpu-moe cells on srv2 (records/measurements/serving-sweep-2026-08-25/): RSS - offloaded expert bytes sat flat at 1.52-1.53 GiB at every setting from 4 to 20 blocks, which is what makes it an intercept rather than a rate. Declared at the same 1.53 for srv1, which has no separate sweep; a differing srv1 reading could not stand beside srv2's, because the product keys this number by engine (llama.cpp), not by rig, and the lab's tests refuse rigs that record different values (tests/lab_numbers.py).

card_remainder_mib.why: The unnamed remainder of the card's non-expert constant `C` after every named term is accounted for, net of the card's idle baseline, on srv1 (src/mcgyvr/serving/vramfit.py's derivation of C; records/measurements/measuring-gaps-2026-09-10/ Q4/Q6, records/measurements/flexibility-2026-09-09/ Q11). It is recorded here because it is per-rig; `C` itself is per (model, serve config) and subsumes it.

It is recorded here because it is per-rig; `C` itself is per (model, serve config) and subsumes it.

engine._doc: Engine-specific measured numbers, shared across rigs. Keyed by engine rather than by host because the figure belongs to the backend, not to the machine it runs on.

warm_decode_class_pct._doc: The percent a unit's warm decode may fall, by the unit's tolerance class (`mcgyvr.fleet.tolerance.tolerance_class`: engine vllm is `vllm`; llama.cpp drafting with the GGUF's own MTP head, `--spec-type draft-mtp`, is `mtp` whether or not experts are on the CPU beside it (owner, 2026-09-16); llama.cpp with experts on the CPU is `cpu_experts`; any other llama.cpp is `llamacpp`): what the fleet lock allows it to lose to NVMe against its no-NVMe baseline, and what a live probe judges its warm decode against. It does not cover prefill, which has its own measured classes in `prefill_class_pct` (owner, 2026-09-15). Owner, 2026-09-15: the measured classes replace the survey's provisional per-engine `warm_decode_pct` (vllm 3.0, llama.cpp 5.0).

vllm.why: The measured class tolerance, records/measurements/fleet-identity-2026-09-11/tolerances.json classes.vllm.tolerance_pct (worst shortfall 0.58% over 15 samples per arm on srv2's 3B and 7B, M1 rule in mcgyvr-lab/records/plans/fleet-identity-measurements-2026-09-11.md).

llamacpp.why: The measured class tolerance, records/measurements/fleet-identity-2026-09-11/tolerances.json classes.llamacpp.tolerance_pct (worst shortfall 0.52% over 15 samples per arm on srv1's Ling-3.0-tiny, M1 rule in mcgyvr-lab/records/plans/fleet-identity-measurements-2026-09-11.md).

cpu_experts.why: The measured class tolerance, records/measurements/fleet-identity-2026-09-11/tolerances.json classes.cpu_experts.tolerance_pct (worst shortfall 47.84% over 15 samples on srv1's Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with experts on the CPU, M1 rule in mcgyvr-lab/records/plans/fleet-identity-measurements-2026-09-11.md).

mtp.why: The measured class tolerance (owner ruling, 2026-09-16, after the mtp-ornith window): worst shortfall 1.63% over 15 warm-decode samples (3 cold starts x 5) of srv2_ornith_mtp — Ornith-1.0-35B Q2_K-AllGPU, stock server-cuda-b10644, --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2, --n-cpu-moe 8, width 1 on srv2 — against the locked 86.78 tok/s (the median of the run medians 85.44 / 86.79 / 86.78), records/measurements/lock-fleets/mtp-ornith/runs.json srv2-08, srv2-16, srv2-24, by the lock-fleets README's rule tol = max(1, ceil(worst shortfall %)). Not cpu_experts' 48%: that was measured on srv1 offload, not this regime.

prefill_class_pct._doc: The percent a unit's prefill may fall below its locked as-run value when a live probe judges it, by the same tolerance class as `warm_decode_class_pct` (`mcgyvr.fleet.tolerance.tolerance_class`). Owner, 2026-09-15: prefill is judged by its own measured class tolerances, not by warm decode's. Measured with NVMe offload disabled by M1's rule in mcgyvr-lab/records/measurements/fleet-identity-prefill-2026-09-12/README.md; vLLM's value is mcgyvr-lab/records/plans/fleet-identity.md §12 'Prefill tolerance — ruled 8%' (B89).

vllm.why: The ruled vLLM prefill tolerance (mcgyvr-lab/records/plans/fleet-identity.md §12, B89): the worst single-sample shortfall after dropping the single restart-tail outlier, rounded up. That is srv2's 3B, records/measurements/fleet-identity-prefill-2026-09-12/results-prefill.json per_unit shortfall_pct 7.86 over 15 samples. The rule's raw classes.vllm.tolerance_pct 22 rests on one 7B sample of 9,460 tok/s, the tail of a restart, which the ruling drops (mcgyvr-lab/records/measurements/fleet-identity-prefill-2026-09-12/README.md).

llamacpp.why: The measured class tolerance, records/measurements/fleet-identity-prefill-2026-09-12/results-prefill.json classes.llamacpp.tolerance_pct (worst shortfall 0.37% over 15 samples on srv1's Ling-3.0-tiny, floored to the rule's 1%).

cpu_experts.why: The measured class tolerance, records/measurements/fleet-identity-prefill-2026-09-12/results-prefill.json classes.cpu_experts.tolerance_pct (worst shortfall 0.13% over 15 samples on srv1's Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with --n-cpu-moe 30, floored to the rule's 1%).

mtp.why: The measured class tolerance (owner ruling, 2026-09-16): records/measurements/lock-fleets/mtp-ornith/prefill-tolerance-mtp.json tolerance_pct, `assemble_evidence.py tolerance --use mtp-ornith --class mtp --unit srv2_ornith_mtp` (worst shortfall 4.29% over 9 prefill samples, 3 cold starts x 3, against the locked 780.77 tok/s). Not cpu_experts' 1%: a live probe judged by that would fail a sample the lock itself accepted.

_procedure_doc: Not read by `mcgyvr.derived` (the product's `src/mcgyvr/derived.py`): it answers from a user's own `numbers.yaml` first and its shipped `data/numbers.json` second. The lab's tests write this file's numbers into that user's file in each test's HOME (`tests/lab_numbers.py`, from `tests/conftest.py`): `engine.warm_decode_class_pct` and `engine.prefill_class_pct` by tolerance class as recorded, and `runtime_resident_gb` once, under the engine the product keys it by, `llama.cpp`, with every rig required to record the same value. In the product, `runtime_resident_gb` is used by `src/mcgyvr/serving/__init__.py` (`_host_gb`) when an MoE spills experts to host RAM; `warm_decode_class_pct` by `src/mcgyvr/cli.py` (`_fleet_lock`, passed to `mcgyvr.fleet.lock.write`), `mcgyvr.fleet.probe` and `mcgyvr.fleet.read`; `prefill_class_pct` by `mcgyvr.fleet.probe` and `mcgyvr.fleet.read`. `card_remainder_mib` is provenance for `src/mcgyvr/serving/vramfit.py`, is not consumed by any code path, and is not written into the user's file: the product ships no such number.
